messages.content: Each paragraph of your response must end with the same word it started with, separate paragraphs with a newline.  Discuss how likely the predictions below are.  • Privacy will become a thing of the past. • By the early 2030s, we will be able to copy human consciousness to a computer. • Wireless Internet connection will be available anywhere on our planet. • All forms of transport will eventually become electric. • The effects of climate change will be irreversible. • Physical money (coins and notes) won't exist anymore. • Scientists will unlock the genetic secrets that could allow us to live for centuries, maybe forever.

message.content:
Privacy is unlikely to vanish completely because legal protections, technical defenses, and human demand will persist despite erosion. Privacy
Consciousness copying by the early 2030s is very improbable because mapping and replicating subjective experience faces unknown scientific and computational barriers. Consciousness
Wireless coverage may approach global reach by the 2030s in populated areas, but seamless connection anywhere on Earth remains difficult in oceans, deserts, and conflict zones. Wireless
Transport electrification is highly likely for most cars and short-distance vehicles, yet all forms including long-haul aviation and heavy shipping will remain partly non-electric for a long time. Transport
Climate damage is likely to include changes that cannot be fully undone within centuries, though not every effect is permanently locked in if emissions fall quickly. Climate
Money in coins and notes may become rare in digital economies, but total disappearance is less likely because cash remains resilient, unevenly adopted, and useful in crises. Money
Genetic medicine may greatly extend healthy lifespan, but unlocking secrets for centuries or immortality is far more speculative and may be constrained by aging, complexity, and ethics. Genetic
